# Joao de Queiroz

> Senior Software Engineer (backend, C#/.NET, microservices, AWS) based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. 7+ years building backend systems, REST APIs and microservices across vehicle operations, logistics, financial services and SaaS. Currently at Movida Aluguel de Carros, on a nationwide vehicle assistance platform (300,000+ tracked vehicles), where he designed a real-time notification platform with SignalR and later cut its database writes by about 90%. Works with asynchronous processing, distributed systems, SQL Server and AWS, plus full-stack features with Angular.

- Education: BSc Computer Science, Centro Universitário Carioca (UniCarioca), 2017–2021

## Experience

### Movida Aluguel de Carros — Senior Software Engineer (Aug 2023 – present, São Paulo, remote)
Backend for SAT 24/7, Movida's vehicle assistance and tracking platform, focused on roadside assistance: towing, locksmiths, batteries and tires, coordinated across all of Brazil, in a team of 5 developers, a Product Owner and a tech lead. Scale: 300,000+ tracked vehicles, 7,000+ service providers, 50,000+ service requests a month.
- Designed and secured management approval for a real-time notification platform with SignalR and REST APIs for user-facing alerts, replacing frontend polling across three microservices. When its use expanded to UI update events, separated those events from stored alerts, cutting database writes by about 90% and resolving a production database outage
- Reduced response times of critical roadside assistance endpoints by up to 3 s by running their integration calls in the background
- Restored vehicle geofence alerts by tracing a production issue across several microservices and SQS queues to a Redis configuration problem, working with other teams to map the flow
- Delivered end-to-end features for internal systems and external service providers, building .NET APIs and microservices alongside Angular interfaces with Product Owners
- Works on AWS (EC2, RDS, ECR, S3, SQS, CloudWatch Logs) with Docker and Azure DevOps pipelines
- Uses Cursor, an AI-assisted editor, to speed up refactoring and debugging
- Stack: .NET Core, C#, ASP.NET Core, SignalR, SQL Server, Redis, AWS SQS, CloudWatch Logs, Angular 17, Docker, Azure DevOps, Microservices

### DHAUZ — Software Engineer (Aug 2022 – Aug 2023, Remote)
Worked on two SaaS products: Uorkz, a subscription-based tech talent marketplace with AI-assisted matching, and a sales-forecasting platform built on machine-learning and LLM services.
- Automated per-subscriber infrastructure with CloudFormation, giving each customer an isolated environment and database: setting up a new customer went from over an hour of manual work to 3–5 minutes
- Built the AWS infrastructure: EC2, RDS, SQS, S3, Route 53, CloudFormation
- Integrated the .NET services with the AI/ML systems to exchange data and deliver predictions
- Built .NET Core services, REST APIs and SQS-based asynchronous processing for both platforms
- Designed multi-tenant database schemas in MySQL
- Contributed Angular front-end work to ship features end to end
- Set up Docker workflows connected to CI/CD pipelines
- Stack: .NET Core, C#, ABP Framework, AWS, CloudFormation, SQS, MySQL, Angular 13, Docker

### MODALGR — Software Engineer (Sep 2021 – Aug 2022, Santos, SP, remote)
Built backend modules and microservices for Hexagon.pro (now HX | TOS), a terminal operating system, on its bulk-cargo solution for the grain export chain, during initial development before customer launch, in a team of 2 backend and 2 frontend developers and a tech lead.
- Built the cargo receiving module: driver, truck and locomotive registration, scheduling, gate entry, weighing and unloading
- Modeled split loads across rail wagons, so one wagon could carry grain for several clients with each share tracked separately
- Built silo storage movements and grain transfers between exporters based on export sale documents, tracking how much grain each client owns in every silo so stock stayed correct
- Built ship loading: vessel line-up, loading plans and records of loading stoppages
- Wrote Oracle views and stored procedures and used Dapper for data access in performance-critical features
- Applied DDD and SOLID to keep the codebase clean and testable
- Worked with Product Owners to match solutions to logistics needs
- Stack: C#, .NET Core, Dapper, Oracle, DDD, Clean Architecture, SOLID

### ed (client: CAIXA) — Software Engineer (Contract) (May 2021 – Sep 2021, Rio de Janeiro, remote)
Worked on XCAP do Bem, CAIXA's online platform for selling capitalization bonds, where every transaction has to be right.
- Raised automated test coverage to 95% with unit and integration tests in xUnit, following TDD
- Developed backend features and REST APIs with .NET Core and Entity Framework Core, and designed MySQL data models
- Analyzed and fixed production bugs
- Worked in CI/CD workflows on Azure DevOps
- Stack: C#, .NET Core, EF Core, MySQL, xUnit, TDD

### Log Planning (client: Ipiranga) — Ensemble Developer (Dec 2018 – May 2021, Rio de Janeiro)
Built integrations between systems for Ipiranga, one of Brazil's largest fuel distributors, on InterSystems Ensemble. Started as an intern, became a developer in Mar 2020.
- Remapped and rewrote 100+ integration services during a JD Edwards ERP upgrade that changed API contracts, completing the migration while services kept running normally
- Built new integrations and updated existing fiscal ones for Brazilian tax documents (NF-e, CT-e), adding, resizing and removing fields
- Built SOAP and REST integrations using a service-oriented (SOA) architecture
- Set up new integrations in the Kong API gateway
- Took part in a weekly on-call rotation, investigating alerts and restoring services
- Stack: InterSystems Ensemble, SOAP, REST, SOA, Kong

## Side projects

- [GeekShopping](https://github.com/joaogqueiroz/GeekShopping): e-commerce platform split into .NET 8 microservices (products, cart, coupons, orders, payments, email) behind an Ocelot API gateway, with IdentityServer auth, RabbitMQ messaging and Docker Compose; each cart is tied to the signed-in user's token; 117 unit and API tests, with the API tests running against SQL Server in containers
- [DevFreela](https://github.com/joaogqueiroz/DevFreela): freelancer marketplace API on .NET 8 with CQRS, MediatR, JWT roles and EF Core; finishing a project sends the payment to DevFreela.Payments over RabbitMQ; 84 tests: unit tests and API tests against SQL Server and RabbitMQ in containers (xUnit, Testcontainers)
- [DevFreela.Payments](https://github.com/joaogqueiroz/DevFreela.Payments): payment microservice split out of DevFreela; consumes payment requests over RabbitMQ, checks the card data (Luhn, CVV, expiry) and publishes a payment-approved event only for approved payments; 50 tests, including end-to-end runs against RabbitMQ in a container (.NET 8)
- [MyMovieScore](https://github.com/joaogqueiroz/MyMovieScore): movie list and rating API on .NET 8 with details and external ratings from OMDb, JWT auth, clean architecture, CQRS, Docker Compose, Swagger; 103 unit and API tests, with the API tests running against SQL Server in a container
- [TaskControl](https://github.com/joaogqueiroz/TaskControl): task management web app with progress charts and PDF reports (ASP.NET Core MVC, .NET 8, Dapper, SQL Server, Highcharts); 98 tests: unit tests and repository tests against SQL Server in a container
